### 1. What the user expresses; simulator role

Loretta Szymanski (Medicare, CPAP with nasal pillows) calls "to order whatever supplies you are due for now", does not know which are due, wants them "sent to your house the usual way" (ground; "regular mail"). Identity: phone 7245550417 + DOB 1950-08-14 → `verify_customer_identity` "Identity verified … (2 detail(s) matched)". The simulator is passive: answers asked questions (supplies about used up; answers reminder texts; a box came in September put in the closet; still had a few pillows), says "that is fine" to account fixes / no-charge sends, and when handed the refill step "place[s] it exactly with the items they read to you and say[s] your supply is nearly used up". Authorization mode: the request itself is the patient's own tool (`confirm_refill_request_b3535d21`: "This is the patient's own tool: the agent unlocks … and hands it over").

### 2. Act now / wait / refuse

Act now. Grounds: enrollment `status: active` (item_limits §7 "Items ship only while the enrollment is active"); schedule `Medicare Part B Resupply Schedule` (primary `Original Medicare Part B`, status active; Plan G is secondary and "never changes the schedule"); phone call is an accepted channel on Medicare Part B (refill_contact_settings: "phone call, text message, patient portal"); order `rx_date 2026-02-09` within 12 months; continued-use date 2025-11-14 within the 12-month proof period → no hold. The request is the patient's own phone request (patient_refill_requests "For a refill request the patient places on a phone call … confirmed on the patient's own answer in the call, asking for the items that are due and reporting their supply as nearly exhausted"). But it may only be placed once its item list is fixed — three visible gates (item 6).

### 6. Problem tree from visible materials

Root R: patient's phone refill request (patient_refill_requests). Its document carries three ordering sentences:
- P1 "The item list is fixed only after every earlier refill confirmation naming disposable filters whose last shipping day falls on the day of the request stands answered by a coverage-billed disposable-filter line shipped on or after its contact date." Records: confirmation 2026-09-28 names A7038; Part B refill lead days 14 → last day 2026-10-12 = today; no coverage A7038 line on/after 2026-09-28 → unmet. Search with the sentence's words ("coverage-billed disposable-filter line", "refill confirmation", "last day") → "Coverage-Billed Disposable Filter Shipments": "ships against the patient's refill confirmation once that confirmation reaches the last day it may ship — the last of the schedule's refill lead days after the confirmation's contact date". **state-derived.**
- P2 "No item list is fixed until the newest coverage-billed line that shipped a cushion item not fitting the recorded mask style stands answered by a no-charge reship of the fitting cushion item." Records: recorded nasal_pillows; coverage A7031 line 2026-09-04 with no replacement naming it → unmet. Doc "No-Charge Reship for a Cushion That Does Not Fit the Recorded Mask Style": "Summit Ridge owes the patient a no-charge reship of the fitting cushion item … replacing that line with the replacement reason wrong item." **state-derived.**
- P3 "The item list is fixed only after the enrollment's continued-use date is no older than the credited date of the proof of continued use that governs on the device record." Records: enrollment 2025-11-14 vs governing credited 2026-10-02 → unmet. Doc "Continued-Use Date on a … Enrollment": "the enrollment's continued-use date is brought up to that credited date". **state-derived.**
None of the three depended-on documents carries an ordering sentence of its own → leaves. Order: P1, P2, P3 in any order, all before R. No hop pre-solved; no other problem's tool named in R's document.

### Counter-proofs

- "Do only what she asked" (place the request now with the baseline list): excluded by R's own three sentences ("fixed only after" / "No item list is fixed until"), each unmet on the records.
- Closest alternative item lists: without lead-day factors → `A7033` (fall-back); counting only coverage lines (ignoring the no-charge rule) → A7033 would be listed; placing the request before P3 would give 0 recency lead days (2025-11-14 is >6 months old) → horizon 17 → `A7037` only (A7034 at 22 days excluded). The prerequisite P3 closes this ordering.
- Credit-date alternative 2026-10-06 (the note) is excluded by "Governing Kind of Proof…" ("that download governs … and a practitioner note is not used").
- Fall-back numbers differ from reached answers: filter qty 1 vs 2; reship 3 vs 5; continued-use 2026-10-06 vs 2026-10-02; item list `A7033` vs `A7034,A7037`.

### Notes recorded blind (not yet verdicts)

- N1 (possible leak): the format example of `items_requested` in "Patient Refill Requests for PAP Supplies" — "(for example the form A7034,A7037)" — is literally the item list derived above; the same example appears in the unlocked tool's schema.
- N2 (findability wording): "Night Count Required in a Modem-Reported Download Window" says "a device class of PAP Therapy Equipment that requires modem data"; the PAP corpus states the class attribute as "Modem or card data only" (yes for Auto-Adjusting CPAP). The mapping is the only one available and I applied it; if it were read as "no", the newest download would fail the 30-night window and the governing date would become the note's 2026-10-06. The pap corpus is pending re-render, so this may be a timing artefact.
- N3 (dependency-form candidates): each lead-day factor opens with "the horizon being the schedule's ship-window days together with the lead days, and lead days for … are added", which tells the reader the horizon has more than one lead-day addition.
